subject.title: fix(backup): sweep stale temp artifacts before creating new backup

question: Should `backup create` startup automatically delete stale OpenClaw-owned staging directories and archive temp files after a grace window?
rationale: The implementation can be repaired mechanically, but deleting old partial backup artifacts is an intentional recovery/debugging policy choice for maintainers.

options.title: Accept Guarded Startup Sweep
options.body: After the matcher is repaired, keep the owner-marker, UUID, directory, and age guards and let backup self-heal stale temp artifacts on later runs.

options.title: Require Explicit Doctor Cleanup
options.body: Move stale backup artifact deletion to a user-invoked doctor/fix path instead of deleting on backup startup.

options.title: Pause Cleanup Work
options.body: Leave the issue and PR open or close the PR until maintainers decide whether partial backup artifacts should ever be auto-deleted.

recommendation.title: Accept Guarded Startup Sweep
recommendation.body: After the matcher is repaired, keep the owner-marker, UUID, directory, and age guards and let backup self-heal stale temp artifacts on later runs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main backup file history and merge context make this the best available owner for current behavior acceptance.
